question: During a repeat lower-segment caesarean section, the greatest risk of intraoperative haemorrhage occurs at the time of uterine incision into the lower segment, particularly when the previous scar is thinned or densely adherent.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Re-read the intraoperative findings section. The entry into a scarred, thinned lower uterine segment is indeed the highest-risk moment for haemorrhage in a repeat LSCS — not closure or placental delivery, though those carry their own risks.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The thinned or fibrotic lower uterine segment from a prior scar is the most hazardous moment — inadvertent extension into uterine vessels or bladder flap injury can cause rapid haemorrhage. This is why careful blunt entry and wide retraction are critical steps the observer should watch for.
